chains.title: FOXA1 loss on the alt allele reduces TOX3 enhancer activity

links.claim: I hypothesize that ref G binds FOXA1 more strongly than alt A. FOXA1 is selected as a candidate because E05 reports MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and high MCF7 expression (88.38 TPM, rank 28/1626); this is occupancy and expression evidence only. No QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific binding data for FOXA1 are provided, so the ref>alt direction is unproven.

The variant lies in the VEP-annotated enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS and 38 bp from the ENCODE dELS EH38E3180851. The variant base itself is not inside a called cCRE, and E03 reports maxima across biosamples, so enhancer activity at this exact base in MCF-7 is inferred rather than shown.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene, 17.6 kb away, and CASC16 overlaps the variant. TOX3 has a general breast-cancer association (E21), but E18a concerns rs4784227 and E18b is locus-level only; no variant-specific evidence shows that rs56007086 regulates TOX3 or CASC16.
MCF-7 is the matching breast cancer biosample and has FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.

This chain predicts that alt A reduces FOXA1-dependent enhancer activity and TOX3 output, contributing to breast cancer risk at 16q12. However, no variant-specific GWAS, eQTL, or literature evidence establishes this direction: E15-E17 and E20 are null, E19 finds no variant-specific literature, and E21 is only a general TOX3-breast-cancer association.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP/CUT&RUN in a heterozygous breast cancer line shows stronger FOXA1 occupancy on ref G than alt A.

chains.title: GATA3 loss on the alt allele alters TOX3 enhancer output

links.claim: I hypothesize that ref G binds GATA3 more strongly than alt A. GATA3 is selected as a candidate because E06 reports MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant and very high MCF7 expression (346.04 TPM, rank 5/1626); this is occupancy and expression evidence only. No QBiC-SELEX model or allele-specific binding data for GATA3 are provided, so the ref>alt direction is unproven.

The variant is in the VEP enhancer ENSR16_9QTBS and near the ENCODE dELS EH38E3180851, consistent with a regulatory element. The variant base is not in a called cCRE, and E03 does not establish MCF-7-specific activity at this base.

TOX3 is the closest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb and CASC16 overlaps the variant. The literature supports TOX3 as a breast-cancer locus generally (E18a, E18b, E21), but not rs56007086 specifically as the causal base regulating TOX3 or CASC16.
GATA3 occupancy at this element is reported in MCF-7, the matching breast cancer biosample.

This chain predicts that alt A weakens GATA3 binding and changes TOX3 enhancer activity in breast cells, contributing to breast cancer risk at 16q12. No variant-specific GWAS, eQTL, or literature evidence establishes this direction; E15-E17 and E20 are null, E19 finds no variant-specific literature, and E21 is only a general TOX3 association.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP/CUT&RUN in a heterozygous breast cancer line shows stronger GATA3 occupancy on ref G than alt A.
